sections.content: How many people are "head teachers and principals"?

54,605 people

were counted on the census as "head teachers and principals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Head teachers and principals direct and co-ordinate the running of schools, colleges and other educational establishments.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 45 to 49 years. Of the whole working population 11% were aged 45 to 49 years. For people working as "head teachers and principals", 20% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "head teachers and principals" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "head teachers and principals" included:

  • information technology directors
  • public relations and communications directors
  • functional managers and directors (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "head teachers and principals" there were more women than men (60.9% compared with 39.1%).

This means "head teachers and principals" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "teaching and other educational professionals".

Men made up 39.1% and women made up 60.9% of "head teachers and principals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "head teachers and principals" included:

  • artists
  • human resource managers and directors
  • bed and breakfast and guest house owners and proprietors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "head teachers and principals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged between 30 and 49 years old, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "head teachers and principals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "head teachers and principals", 6.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (92.2% compared with 7.8%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (92.1%) than self-employed (7.9%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
